comments.text:
Some notes about the Coast Guard from someone with 20+ years of experience. I'm not a rescue swimmer, but I have worked with them.

The CG has rates which are specialized job fields, some are broad, but ASTs (rescue swimmer) are highly specialized. It's a difficult job to get into. They get some medical training, but they're not medics as their first job. It's takes a lot of physical fitness and training to be able to haul people out of the water and into those baskets, especially in rough water. A lot of their training is for that skill. You can find YouTube videos with more details, it's very impressive.

Health Services techs are the medics. Anytime there was a HS# next to someone's name, that's their job. They get more medical training, of course, and work in a variety of areas.

There's also AMT, Aviation Maintenance Techs and they manage the maintenance and operation of the helio.

The pilots are officers. AMT, AST, HS, enlisted.
